summary: In this episode, Fathers Andrew Stephen Damick and Stephen De Young tackle the popular internet meme that Christmas and Christianity are derived from the ancient Roman mystery cult of Mithras. They begin by tracing the historical origins of the god Mithra from Hittite treaties and the Rig Veda, showing his role as a covenant mediator in Indo-Persian religion. They then examine Roman Mithraism as a distinct phenomenon that emerged in the mid-to-late first century AD, primarily among Roman soldiers, and discuss its archaeology, iconography, and rituals, including the tauroctony and the sacred meal. The hosts critically assess the claims made by Jesus mythicists and internet memes, demonstrating that many parallels are based on misinformation or lack of evidence. They conclude with a broader reflection on the importance of critical thinking, the uniqueness of Christianity, and the dangers of ecumenical movements that downplay doctrinal differences.

entities.title: Mithras
entities.summary: A god in Indo-Persian religion, later central to Roman Mithraism, associated with covenants and the sun.

entities.title: Father Andrew Stephen Damick
entities.summary: Orthodox priest and co-host of the podcast, known for his theological insights and humor.

entities.title: Father Stephen De Young
entities.summary: Orthodox priest and co-host, an expert in biblical and ancient Near Eastern studies.

entities.title: Mithraea
entities.summary: Caves or artificial caves used for Mithraic worship, found across the Roman Empire.

entities.title: Celsus
entities.summary: A second-century pagan philosopher who wrote against Christianity; his work is known through Origen's response.

concepts.title: Mithraism
concepts.summary: A Roman mystery cult centered on the god Mithras, popular among soldiers, with rituals in underground caves, including a sacred meal and initiation grades.

concepts.title: Tauroctony
concepts.summary: The central image of Mithras slaying a bull, symbolizing cosmic creation and renewal, with astrological elements.

concepts.title: Mystery Cult
concepts.summary: A religious group with secret rituals and initiations, often involving personal salvation and esoteric knowledge.

concepts.title: Hypostasis
concepts.summary: In ancient paganism, a localized embodiment of a deity; used by modern scholars to describe how Mithras could be an aspect of the sun god.

concepts.title: Jesus Mythicism
concepts.summary: The fringe belief that Jesus never existed, often used to argue Christianity borrowed from pagan myths like Mithras.

claims.text: Roman Mithraism emerged around the time of Nero, thus postdating Christianity by at least 30 years.
There is no evidence that Mithras was born on December 25; the claim is based on nothing.
Mithras was born from a rock, not a virgin birth, and the claim of a virgin birth is a distortion.
Mithras had two attendants, not twelve disciples; the claim of twelve disciples is baseless.
There is no evidence that Mithras died and rose again; this is a fabrication of modern mythicists.
Christianity is not derived from Mithraism; the parallels are superficial and often based on misinformation.
